SchematicOptions.description:
The Project's schematic options: how Nets are named, Ports cross-referenced and Not
Fitted Components drawn.

allow_ports_to_name_nets.description:
Allow Ports to Name Nets. Off, a Port still joins its Net across sheets but never
names it.

append_sheet_numbers.description:
Append Sheet Numbers to Local Nets: every Local Net named by a Net Label gets the
board name `<name>_<n>`, `n` being its sheet's number. Sheets keep showing the plain
name.

cross_reference_styles.description: The Project's cross-reference styles, unless it follows the Preferences.

cross_references.description:
Automatic Cross References: each Port shows where its partners are, such as

cross_references_follow_preferences.description:

Preferences instead of [`SchematicOptions::cross_reference_styles`]. Off by default.

not_fitted_display.description:
How a Not Fitted Component is drawn on the canvas and in the PDF: `cross` (the
default), `mesh` or `none`.

power_port_names_priority.description:
Power Port Names Take Priority: a Power Port's name beats a Net Label's, giving
Power Port > Net Label > Port > auto-name. Off by default (Net Label > Power Port >
Port > auto-name).

InDocument27.description:
An object stored in a Document, with the Document it lives in. The Document is not
serialised: object views and files say where an object is in their own way.

clearance.description:
The gap kept to other Nets' copper. Left out, the clearance rule applies; set, the
larger of it and the rule applies.

follows_outline.description:
Whether the outline is the Board Outline, following its later edits; the fill
keeps the edge clearance from it. Left out when false.

layer.description: The copper Layer it fills.

min_island_area.description:
Pieces of fill smaller than this, in square nanometres, are dropped, connected or
not.

min_width.description:
The narrowest copper the fill may leave: thinner necks are removed. Left out, the
Net's `track_width` minimum.

name.description:
Its typed name, unique on the board. Left out, it shows a name derived from the
board's [`ZoneNameScheme`], which is never stored.

net.description: Its PCB Net; left out for a fill on no Net.

pour_over.description: How the fill treats same-Net Zones and Tracks.

priority.description:
Where Zones overlap, the higher priority fills first and the others keep clear
of it.

remove_unconnected.description:
Whether pieces of fill that touch no copper of the Net are dropped. No effect on a
Zone with no Net.

shelved.description:
Whether it is shelved: kept in the file but hidden from the canvas and skipped by
fill, DRC, connectivity and outputs. Left out when false.

vertices.description:
The outline the fill stays inside; the last vertex joins the first. Empty while
the Zone [follows the Board Outline](Self::follows_outline).

width.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

zone_connection.description: How Zone fills of its Net join it. Each value left out inherits.

paper ([`BorderZones::for_paper`]), never stored.

drawing_number.description: The sheet's drawing number; empty by default.

revision.description: The sheet's own revision. Empty, the title block shows the Project's.

title_block.description: The built-in title block, on by default.

oneOf.description: A clock input's wedge.

One of the nine anchor points of a text block: its corners, the middles of its sides
and its centre. Top is the first line's capital height, bottom the last line's
baseline, and middle halfway between them.

side.description: The board face, for sided Layers; left out for the others.

layer.description: The Layer's name, so the override carries between boards and Projects.

name.description: The file name to write that Layer's Gerber as.

LayerKind.description: What a Layer is for. Copper and the sided kinds come with a [`Side`].

LayerSpan.description:
The copper Layers a Via joins: every copper Layer from `from` to `to` in Layer order.
`from` is the upper Layer, so a through Via is stored top to bottom. `from` is also the
side it is drilled from, which matters only once blind Vias come.

as Reject.

library_field_missing.description: A field in the Library and not on the Component.

locally_edited.description: A changed default the Component has its own value for.

remove_missing_footprints.description: Footprints gone from the Library leave the alternates.

step.description: The increase from one row to the next.

The cell starts as Update: the Component takes the new default.

Nothing extra: drawn like any other Component.

upwards too, so "descending Y" starts at the top.

commands.description: Runs an Output Job: refills stale Zones, plots the Gerber X2 files (top and bottom copper, Solder Mask, Paste and Silkscreen, the Board Outline as the Profile; an empty Silkscreen or Paste is left out and listed in `skipped`) and the Excellon drill files (plated and non-plated) and writes them with the CSV BOM and CPL (columns from the job's Fab Preset; Not Fitted and Mechanical Parts left out) and their zip, `<project>-<job>.zip`, to the job's destination (default `outputs/<job>/`), replacing the last run's files. Gerber, drill and CPL share one origin: the board's own zero for an `absolute` preset, and for a `relative` one the Output Origin, or the lower-left of the Board Outline while none is placed. The checks that block read only the job's PCB: duplicate Designators, an open Board Outline, a Footprint the PCB cannot resolve and a coordinate beyond ±2147.483647 mm (`coordinate_out_of_range`) block the run (`rejected`, `details.blockers`). Other problems, such as an out-of-sync PCB or a Component without a Footprint, are listed as `warnings`. Long-running: reports progress and can be cancelled.

Wiring.description:
How edits normalise the Wires they touch: the four wiring Preferences, and the snap
grid that converting a cross-junction offsets by. A Command given no `wiring` uses
these defaults, not the user's Preferences, so its result is the same on every
machine; the app passes the Preferences. A field left out takes its default.

break_wires_at_autojunctions.description:
Break Wires At Autojunctions (on): a Wire splits at each Junction on its interior.
Off, it stays one Wire through the Junction.

components_cut_wires.description:
Components Cut Wires (on; needs Optimize Wires): when two or more Pins of a
placed, moved or pasted Unit land on one straight stretch of a Wire, the pieces
between them are removed unless something else connects there. Off, the Pins
connect and the part may be shorted.

convert_cross_junctions.description:
Convert Cross-Junctions (on): a Wire that would make a 4-way is offset into two
adjacent 3-ways, one snap grid apart. Off, the 4-way stays as drawn.

optimize_wires.description:
Optimize Wires (on): overlapping collinear Wires merge, and so do collinear Wires
meeting end to end with nothing else at that point; collinear vertices inside a
Wire are removed. Off, Wires stay as drawn.

snap_grid.description: The snap grid a converted cross-junction is offset by; 50 mil by default.

keep_connections.description: Keep connections as a drag does. Off by default (detached).

objects.description:
The objects to align, by UUID, all on one sheet. Each one's extent is its Pins
and body drawing (Units), its vertices (Wires), its ends (graphics) or its point (labels,
markers, Ports, Power Ports, text).

commands.title: Place Component

commands.description: Gives Components another Part, from any registered Library. Each keeps its UUID (so Sync swaps its Footprint in place), Designator, Not Fitted, Unit positions and field positions. `keep_fields`: `edited` (default) keeps values that differ from the old Part's defaults, `all` keeps every value, `none` takes the new Part's. Component Type is always the new Part's; In BOM and In CPL follow `keep_fields`. The Footprint is the same one by UUID, then by name, then the new default, unless `footprint` names one. Units match by index, and a placed Unit with no match blocks that Component. Refused for a Part with no Symbol. Wires never move. Preview it with `schematic.component.replace_preview`.

Every value the Component holds stays; only fields it has no value for take the new
Part's defaults.
Every value takes the new Part's default, and fields the new Part lacks go.

parameters; when given, a replace that no longer matches fails with `conflict`.

commands.description: Applies the update `schematic.component.update_preview` showed, given its `preview_hash` and the same parameters; fails with `conflict` when the result no longer matches. Excluded Components stay as they are, and cells start as the preview says unless `excluded_cells` or `updated_cells` override them (Locked cells cannot be). the update removes, because it changes that Footprint's hash. Omitted when none.

reason.description: For Source Missing: what is missing.

library_field_missing.description: A field in the Library and not on the Component.

locally_edited.description: A changed default the Component has its own value for.

preserve_field_visibility.description: Which fields show stays as it is; off, the Designator and value show.

remove_missing_footprints.description: Footprints gone from the Library leave the alternates.

LocalEdit.description: One property of one Pad or graphic that differs from the copy it came from.

edited.description: The edited value; left out when it isn't set.

graphic.description: The graphic, for a graphic edit.

number.description: The Pad's number, for a Pad edit.

original.description: The original value; left out when it wasn't set.

pad.description: The Pad, for a Pad edit.

property.description: The property, as the file names it; `graphic` for a graphic added or deleted whole.

LocallyEdited.description: A changed default where the Component holds a value of its own.

oneOf.description: The cell starts as Reject: the Component keeps its value.

PartChange.description: One difference an update makes, under the aspect that brings it.

oneOf.description: Fields: the Part was renamed.

Symbol: the Symbol changed; `name` is its name after, and `graphics` whether its
drawing changed.
Symbol: a Unit new in the Symbol. It appears as unplaced.

Symbol: a Unit gone from the Symbol. A placed one blocks the Component until the
user deletes that Unit.

Symbol: a Pin added, removed, renamed, retyped or moved, matched by number within
its Unit. On a placed Unit, `leaves` and `joins` name the Nets the Pin leaves and
joins: Wires never move, so a moved Pin may leave its Net.

Footprints: an alternate added, removed or changed. On a changed one, the Pad
numbers added or removed and the Pads (by number) moved or resized. The PCB gets
the change through Sync, not through the update.
Footprints: the alternates kept are in a new order; the first is the default.
Footprints: the pin-pad map overrides, old and new.
Footprints: the Component's Footprint choice changes (`null` = none).

pins.description: Pins mapped to other Pads, or to several, sorted by Pin number.

unconnected.description: Pad numbers deliberately left unconnected, sorted.

components.description: The Components in scope that are not Up to Date, by Designator in natural order.

commands.title: Preview Update from Library

commands.description: Copies the selected objects, with the part-table entries their Units use, and returns them as a clipboard for schematic.paste. Changes nothing.

objects.description: The objects to copy, by UUID, all on one sheet.

ComponentRef.description:
Which Component an object refers to: its UUID, after the Sheet Instance path that
leads to it. In v0.1 sheets are flat and the path is always empty.

path.description: The Sheet Instances from the top sheet down. Empty in v0.1.

ComponentType.description:
What kind of part a Part is: it decides what the Part needs and where it may be
placed, and gives the defaults for In BOM and In CPL, which are separate flags.

oneOf.description:
An ordinary part: it needs a Symbol and a Footprint, and reaches the board only
through Sync.

A part with a Symbol, a Footprint or both, such as a screw, a heat sink or a
mounting hole. It may be placed straight onto the board.

A deliberate short between Nets, made of touching Pads. It syncs like a Standard
part and is never Not Fitted.

ConnectionStyle.description: How a fill meets a Pad or Via.

oneOf.description: Through spokes across a clear ring, so the Pad solders easily.
The fill runs straight into it.
The fill keeps the gap clear and doesn't connect.

Corner.description: A corner of a Pad, in its own frame (+y up).

EditedFrom.description:
The copy a Locally Edited Footprint came from (ADR-0013): that copy's UUID in the same
part table and its content hash, which Sync compares with the schematic's copy.

FieldText.description:
Where a field moved by hand sits: an offset from the Symbol origin in the Symbol's
own frame (so rotating or mirroring the Unit carries it along), and its text height
when it is not the default.

size.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

Fields.description: A Part's default fields, copied onto each Component placed from it.

custom.description: Free-form fields, such as `LCSC` or `DigiKey`, in the user's order.

Footprint.description:
The physical land pattern of a part. Coordinates are relative to its origin, and its
zero orientation follows IPC-7351.

generator.description:
The generator Command and resolved params that made it. It lives only in the
Library's `.redafp`: the copies Documents hold, and their hashes, leave it out.

graphics.description: Silkscreen, Courtyard and Assembly drawing, sorted by UUID.

height.description: The part's greatest height above the board, when known. Generators fill it in.

pads.description: Sorted by UUID. Numbers may repeat: Pads that share a number belong to one Pin.

provenance.description: Where an imported Footprint came from. Elements made in REDA have none.

texts.description: The field texts it draws, such as its Designator and value, sorted by UUID.

FootprintCopy.description:
A copy of a Library Footprint on a sheet, shared by every part-table entry that lists
it. Keyed by the Footprint's UUID plus [`FootprintCopy::hash`].

edited_from.description: On a PCB's Locally Edited Footprint: the copy it was edited from. Never on a sheet.

hash.description: The content hash of the Footprint, as copied.

FootprintGenerator.description:
The command and params that generated a Footprint, every value resolved, so running
them again gives the same Footprint unless the generator itself changed.

FootprintGraphic.description: One shape a Footprint draws on a non-copper Layer.

fill.description: Whether a closed shape is filled.

width.description: The stroke width.

FootprintLayer.description: The Layers a Footprint draws on besides copper.

FootprintText.description: One field text of a Footprint, on a Silkscreen or Assembly Layer.

at.description:
The text anchor, relative to the Footprint origin; `style.justify` says how the

field.description:
The field it shows: `Designator`, `Value` or any field name. A field the Component
does not have draws nothing.

rotation.description: An angle in integer millidegrees, counter-clockwise. Serialises as a bare integer.

Hole.description:
A drilled hole: round when `width == height`, otherwise a slot along the longer side.
Sizes are the finished diameter.

height.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

rotation.description: Turns a slot in the Pad's frame, counter-clockwise.

tolerance.description:
The allowed deviation from the finished size. Stored and shown; it changes no
geometry.

width.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

minus.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

plus.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

InsideEdge.description: A Pin decoration just inside the body edge.

oneOf.description: A clock input's wedge.

expansion.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

oneOf.description: An inversion circle.

The active-low output flag.

Pad.description: A copper area, with or without a hole, of a Footprint.

at.description:
The Pad's anchor, relative to the Footprint origin: the hole sits there, Tracks
connect there and the Pad turns about it.

corner_ratio.description:
How round the corners of a `rounded_rect`, or the uncut corners of a

corners.description:
Which corners are rounded (`rounded_rect`) or chamfered (`chamfered_rect`), in the

hole.description: A round hole when width equals height, otherwise a slot. SMD Pads have none.

paste.description: An SMD Pad's paste opening; omitted, it inherits the board's rule.

symbol.description: Mechanical Parts may have none; Standard and Net Tie Parts need one.

with the same pair, and a changed Part gets an entry of its own.

A Wire: a polyline at any angle through its `vertices`, in order, at least two. It

Wiring.description:
How edits normalise the Wires they touch: the four wiring Preferences, and the snap
grid that converting a cross-junction offsets by. A Command given no `wiring` uses
these defaults, not the user's Preferences, so its result is the same on every
machine; the app passes the Preferences. A field left out takes its default.

break_wires_at_autojunctions.description:
Break Wires At Autojunctions (on): a Wire splits at each Junction on its interior.
Off, it stays one Wire through the Junction.

components_cut_wires.description:
Components Cut Wires (on; needs Optimize Wires): when two or more Pins of a
placed, moved or pasted Unit land on one straight stretch of a Wire, the pieces
between them are removed unless something else connects there. Off, the Pins
connect and the part may be shorted.

convert_cross_junctions.description:
Convert Cross-Junctions (on): a Wire that would make a 4-way is offset into two
adjacent 3-ways, one snap grid apart. Off, the 4-way stays as drawn.

optimize_wires.description:
Optimize Wires (on): overlapping collinear Wires merge, and so do collinear Wires
meeting end to end with nothing else at that point; collinear vertices inside a
Wire are removed. Off, Wires stay as drawn.

snap_grid.description: The snap grid a converted cross-junction is offset by; 50 mil by default.

objects.description: The objects to cut, by UUID, all on one sheet.

wiring.description: How the Wires this edit touches are normalised; the fixed defaults when left out.

mask.description: Per-side solder-mask expansion or tenting; omitted values inherit the board's rule.

offset.description: Where the copper sits relative to `at`, in the Pad's frame. Left out, on it.

paste.description: An SMD Pad's paste opening; omitted, it inherits the board's rule.

rotation.description: An angle in integer millidegrees, counter-clockwise. Serialises as a bare integer.

side.description:
The side of an SMD Pad, in the Footprint's frame. Left out, the top. Pads with a
hole have none: their copper is on every Layer.

width.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

zone_connection.description: How Zone fills of its Net join it. Each value left out inherits.

oneOf.description: A rectangle with rounded corners: `corner_ratio`, on `corners`.

A rectangle with `corners` cut off by `chamfer_ratio`, the others rounded by
`corner_ratio`. An octagon is one.

Part.description:
A Library definition that binds a Symbol to its alternate Footprints, with default
fields, a Component Type and the In BOM and In CPL defaults.

footprints.description: The alternate Footprints, in order; the first is the default.

in_bom.description:
Whether its Components go into the BOM, by default. Stored explicitly, never
inferred from the type.

in_cpl.description:
Whether its Components go into the CPL, by default. Stored explicitly, never
inferred from the type.

provenance.description: Where an imported Part came from. Elements made in REDA have none.

symbol.description: Mechanical Parts may have none; Standard and Net Tie Parts need one.

PartEntry.description:
One entry of a sheet's part table: a literal copy of a Library Part with its Symbol,
placed once per sheet and shared by every Unit placed from it. It is keyed by the
Part's UUID ([`Part::uuid`]) plus [`PartEntry::hash`]: a sheet never holds two entries
with the same pair, and a changed Part gets an entry of its own.

footprints.description: The sheet's [`FootprintCopy`] of each alternate, in the order of `part.footprints`.

hash.description: The content hash of the Part with its Symbol and Footprints, as copied.

uuid.description: The entry's own UUID, which Units point at.

expansion.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

corner_ratio.description: Thousandths of a percent of half the shorter side: 100000 is fully round.

height.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

width.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

Pin.description: A connection point of a Symbol.

at.description: The connection end of the Pin, relative to the Symbol origin.

description.description: What the Pin is for, shown on hover. Left out when empty.

inside_edge.description: The glyph drawn just inside the body edge, such as a clock wedge.

length.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

name_visible.description: Whether the Pin's name is drawn.

number.description:
Unique across the Symbol; Pins map to the Pads with the same number unless the
Part overrides it.

number_visible.description: Whether the Pin's number is drawn.

outside_edge.description: The glyph drawn just outside the body edge, such as an inversion dot.

rotation.description: The direction from the connection end towards the body, counter-clockwise from +x.

PinMap.description:
The Part's exceptions to the implicit map, where a Pin connects to the Pads with its
own number.

pins.description: Pins mapped to other Pads, or to several, sorted by Pin number.

unconnected.description: Pad numbers deliberately left unconnected, sorted.

PinPads.description: One Pin mapped to an explicit set of Pads.

PinType.description: A Pin's electrical type, which ERC checks.

Point.description: A position on a Schematic Sheet or the PCB Document, which share one coordinate type.

x.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

y.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

Port.description:
A named, directional marker that joins the Wire (or Pin) under `at` to every Port of
the same name on any Schematic Sheet of the Project.

at.description: The connection point.

hide_cross_reference.description: Hides the Port's cross-reference note, when the Project shows them.

rotation.description: Counter-clockwise; only how the Port is drawn.

PortDirection.description:
Which way a Port's signal flows. It only changes how the Port is drawn and checked;
every direction connects the same way.

PowerPort.description:
A named symbol, such as GND or 3V3, that joins the Wire (or Pin) under `at` to the
Project-wide Net of that name on every Schematic Sheet.

at.description: The connection point.

hide_name.description: Draws the symbol without its name. The name still joins the Net.

rotation.description: Counter-clockwise; only how the symbol is drawn.

PowerPortStyle.description: The fixed, built-in look of a Power Port.

oneOf.description: A horizontal bar, for positive rails.
Three shrinking bars.
A downward triangle.
Ground bars with diagonal strokes.

Provenance.description:
Where an imported Library element came from, kept with the element so its terms travel
with it: vendor parts stay under the vendor's terms after import.

copyright.description: Copyright lines found in the imported files, kept verbatim.

service.description: The service the files came from, such as `SnapMagic`, or `Unknown`.

terms_url.description: The service's terms of use, when known.

Shape.description: A drawn shape. Lines, arcs and outlines are stroked with the graphic's width.

oneOf.description: An axis-aligned rectangle between two opposite corners.

The arc from `start` around `center`, sweeping `sweep` counter-clockwise (negative
is clockwise).

sweep.description: An angle in integer millidegrees, counter-clockwise. Serialises as a bare integer.

radius.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

oneOf.description: A closed polygon through its corners.

at.description: The text's anchor.

rotation.description: An angle in integer millidegrees, counter-clockwise. Serialises as a bare integer.

size.description: The text height.

SheetGraphic.description: A free line or rectangle drawn on a sheet. It has no electrical meaning.

oneOf.description: A straight line, at any angle.
An axis-aligned rectangle between two opposite corners.

SheetText.description: Free text drawn on a sheet. It has no electrical meaning.

at.description: The anchor point, which [`SheetText::justify`] places on the text block.

height.description: The capital height.

justify.description: Which of the block's nine points sits on `at`; `bottom_left` by default.

rotation.description: Counter-clockwise about `at`.

text.description: The text; `\n` starts a new line.

Side.description: Which face of the board a sided Layer is on.

Symbol.description: The schematic representation of a part: its Units, each with its Pins and graphics.

designator_prefix.description: The Designator prefix of Components placed from it, such as `R` or `U`.

graphics.description:
The body drawing of every Unit, sorted by UUID; [`SymbolGraphic::unit`] says which
Unit it belongs to.

pins.description: Every Pin of every Unit, sorted by UUID; [`Pin::unit`] says which Unit it is on.

provenance.description: Where an imported Symbol came from. Elements made in REDA have none.

units.description: In order: A, B, C… A single-unit Symbol has exactly one.

SymbolGraphic.description: One shape of a Symbol Unit's body.

fill.description: Whether a closed shape is filled.

unit.description: The Unit it is drawn on.

width.description: The stroke width.

TextJustify.description: How a text block sits on its anchor. Bottom is the last line's baseline.

margin.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

TextStyle.description: The shared style of free PCB text and Footprint field text.

font.description: The named family. A missing family draws as bundled Noto Sans.

height.description: Capital height.

thickness.description: Stroke-font pen width; outline fonts ignore it.

Unit.description: One independently placeable section of a Symbol.

name.description: Such as `A`, or `Power` for a power section.

UnitInstance.description:
One placed Unit of a Component. Every Unit of a Component carries the same copy of the
Component's data; Commands keep the copies equal.

at.description: Where the Symbol origin sits on the sheet.

designator_locked.description: Locked against Re-annotate, which then leaves the Designator as it is.

field_text.description:
The fields moved by hand on this Unit, one entry per field, sorted by field name
(the names of `visible_fields`). A field with no entry is autopositioned. Each
Unit has its own.

footprint.description: The chosen Footprint: the UUID of one of the Part's alternates, if it has any.

in_bom.description: Whether the Component goes into the BOM; copied from the Part, then editable.

in_cpl.description: Whether the Component goes into the CPL; copied from the Part, then editable.

locked_fields.description:
The Locked Fields, by name: Update from Library leaves them as they are, though
they can still be edited by hand. Every Unit of a Component carries the same set.

mirror.description: Mirrored left to right before rotating.

part.description: The part-table entry on this sheet it was placed from.

rotation.description: An angle in integer millidegrees, counter-clockwise. Serialises as a bare integer.

visible_fields.description:
The fields drawn on the sheet, by name: `designator`, a built-in field's stored name
(such as `value`) or a free-form field's name. Designator and value by default.

Wire.description:
A Wire: a polyline at any angle through its `vertices`, in order, at least two. It
connects where an end touches a Pin's connection point or any point of another Wire,
and anywhere along it that it passes over a Pin's connection point, a Port, a Power
Port or a Net Label. Two Wires crossing mid-span never connect.

ZoneConnection.description:
How a Zone fill joins a Pad of its own Net. Each value left out inherits from the
`zone_connection` rule.

angle.description: 0, 45 or 90 degrees in the Pad's frame.

gap.description: The clear ring around a relieved or unconnected Pad.

spoke_width.description: A length or coordinate in integer nanometres. Serialises as a bare integer.

result.description:
Copied sheet objects, as `schematic.copy` and `schematic.cut` return them and
`schematic.paste` takes them. Treat it as opaque.

footprints.description: The Footprint copies those entries list.

origin.description: The lower-left corner of the copied objects' extent; pasting puts it at `at`.

parts.description: The part-table entries the copied Units use.

commands.title: Cut

commands.description: Deletes the selected objects from their sheets. Part-table entries no remaining Unit uses, and Footprint copies no remaining entry lists, go with them.

Length.description: A length: integer nanometres, or a number and a unit (nm, um, mm, mil or in) such as "1.27mm", "10mil" or "0.5in".

oneOf.description: Nanometres.
A number and a unit: nm, um, mm, mil or in.

Wiring.description:
How edits normalise the Wires they touch: the four wiring Preferences, and the snap
grid that converting a cross-junction offsets by. A Command given no `wiring` uses
these defaults, not the user's Preferences, so its result is the same on every
machine; the app passes the Preferences. A field left out takes its default.

break_wires_at_autojunctions.description:
Break Wires At Autojunctions (on): a Wire splits at each Junction on its interior.
Off, it stays one Wire through the Junction.

components_cut_wires.description:
Components Cut Wires (on; needs Optimize Wires): when two or more Pins of a
placed, moved or pasted Unit land on one straight stretch of a Wire, the pieces
between them are removed unless something else connects there. Off, the Pins
connect and the part may be shorted.

convert_cross_junctions.description:
Convert Cross-Junctions (on): a Wire that would make a 4-way is offset into two
adjacent 3-ways, one snap grid apart. Off, the 4-way stays as drawn.

optimize_wires.description:
Optimize Wires (on): overlapping collinear Wires merge, and so do collinear Wires
meeting end to end with nothing else at that point; collinear vertices inside a
Wire are removed. Off, Wires stay as drawn.

snap_grid.description: The snap grid a converted cross-junction is offset by; 50 mil by default.

objects.description:
The objects to delete, by UUID: Units, Wires, Net Labels, No-Connect Markers,
Ports, Power Ports, text and graphics, on any sheets.

wiring.description: How the Wires this edit touches are normalised; the fixed defaults when left out.

result.description: What `schematic.delete` removed.

deleted.description:
The objects deleted, including the part-table entries and Footprint copies that no
Unit uses any more.

result.title: DeleteResult

grid that converting a cross-junction offsets by. A Command given no `wiring` uses

adjacent 3-ways, one snap grid apart. Off, the 4-way stays as drawn.

meeting end to end with nothing else at that point; collinear vertices inside a

Wiring.description:
How edits normalise the Wires they touch: the four wiring Preferences, and the snap
grid that converting a cross-junction offsets by. A Command given no `wiring` uses
these defaults, not the user's Preferences, so its result is the same on every
machine; the app passes the Preferences. A field left out takes its default.

break_wires_at_autojunctions.description:
Break Wires At Autojunctions (on): a Wire splits at each Junction on its interior.
Off, it stays one Wire through the Junction.

components_cut_wires.description:
Components Cut Wires (on; needs Optimize Wires): when two or more Pins of a
placed, moved or pasted Unit land on one straight stretch of a Wire, the pieces
between them are removed unless something else connects there. Off, the Pins
connect and the part may be shorted.

convert_cross_junctions.description:
Convert Cross-Junctions (on): a Wire that would make a 4-way is offset into two
adjacent 3-ways, one snap grid apart. Off, the 4-way stays as drawn.

optimize_wires.description:
Optimize Wires (on): overlapping collinear Wires merge, and so do collinear Wires
meeting end to end with nothing else at that point; collinear vertices inside a
Wire are removed. Off, Wires stay as drawn.

snap_grid.description: The snap grid a converted cross-junction is offset by; 50 mil by default.

angle.description:
Counter-clockwise; a quarter turn by default. Any angle turns Units, Wires, labels,
Ports, Power Ports and text; rectangles turn only in quarter turns.

center.description:
The point to turn about. By default a lone object's own origin (a Unit's origin, a
label's or text's point), else the centre of the selection's extent.

keep_connections.description:
Keep connections as a drag does: attached Wires follow the moved Pins. Off by
default (detached).

commands.description: Applies the Change List of `sync.preview` to the PCB Document in one transaction, leaving out the `exclude`d changes and every change that requires one. New Footprints go into a fresh cluster outside the Board Outline (at the origin with no outline), grouped by sheet and sorted by Designator. Problem rows are skipped, with the changes requiring them, and reported in `left_out`. Fails with `conflict` when the Change List no longer matches `hash`, and is rejected while a `duplicate_nets` Violation stands (with the check Off or the Violation waived, Nets with one board name merge into one PCB Net).

exclude.description:
Ids of changes to leave out; the changes that require them are left out too.
Problem rows are always left out.

hash.description: The `hash` of the previewed Change List.

leads to it. In v0.1 sheets are flat and the path is always empty.

result.description: What `sync.apply` did.

applied.description: The ids of the changes carried out, in list order.

footprints.description: The Footprints added, in the order they were placed (sheet, then Designator).

left_out.description:
The ids left out (excluded, Problem rows, or depending on one of those), in list
order. They show up again in the next preview.

nets.description: The Nets added, in Change List order.

commands.title: Update PCB from Schematic

commands.description: Compares the Schematic Sheets with the PCB Document and returns the pending Change List, one group per kind of change in a fixed order (add_components, remove_components, change_footprints, designators, fields, component_types, in_bom, in_cpl, not_fitted, add_nets, rename_nets, remove_nets, pad_nets). Each change has a stable id, the ids it requires (unticking a change also unticks every change that requires it) and a status: `ok`, `note` (applies; `message` says what follows) or `problem` (can't apply; `message` says why). `count` is the out-of-sync count and leaves out Problem rows; `hash` goes to `sync.apply`; `duplicate_nets` is set while that ERC Violation stands and blocks the apply. Nothing is stored.

params.description: Params for a Command that takes none: accepts `{}` (or `null`) and refuses any field.

pad.description: The Pad of the (new) Footprint.

What kind of part a Part is: it decides what the Part needs and where it may be

through Sync.

A part with a Symbol, a Footprint or both, such as a screw, a heat sink or a
mounting hole. It may be placed straight onto the board.

A deliberate short between Nets, made of touching Pads. It syncs like a Standard
